items.area: R1 — D61 cleanup (done before planning)
items.description: "D61 cleanup (ANS-103, due from 2026-09-25 19:45Z): the migrated apps' HelmCharts content, their Helm release Secrets, DockerImages' `cicd.helmDeploy()` stage and HelmCharts' `gitToken` injection." Only the three parked apps (design-assistant, open-webui, shell) keep `_shared/` and values. (2) HelmCharts' `Jenkinsfile` injects no `gitToken`. (3) DockerImages has no `helmDeploy`. (4) No migrated app has a `sh.helm.release.v1.*` Secret left on prd. The one Helm release Secret on prd is `sh.helm.release.v1.argocd-prd.v1`, from Argo's own bootstrap install on 2026-09-04, and it is not a migrated app's. All four were verified 2026-09-26.
items.rationale: Re-checked all four parts live on 2026-09-26. (1) `find configs/prd -type f ! -name release.yaml` in /work/HelmCharts lists only the parked apps' files (design-assistant x4 stages + _shared, open-webui, shell); 56 release.yaml, the 6 without `reconciler: argo-cd` are exactly those parked stages. (4) `kubectl get secrets -A --field-selector type=helm.sh/release.v1` (names only, no values) returns one Secret, argocd-prd/sh.helm.release.v1.argocd-prd.v1, Argo's own bootstrap install. items.area: R5 — recommend-resources has a home and a way to run
items.description: "We need to figure out how to run recommend resources. I'm guessing the answer will be to just clone all deploy repos and do this using a script. I'm also guessing that we don't yet have a home for this tool." Per the D3 ruling, recommend-resources is a script under Ansible's `support/`, beside argo-migrate, run from this environment. It enumerates the deploy repos from ArgoCDDeploy's registry, clones them to a scratch directory, reads Prometheus at `http://prometheus.home`, and rewrites the resources in each registry app-stage's values file (`config/prd/values.yaml` for every prd stage). It reads nothing from HelmCharts; the nine container-to-values-path maps HelmCharts kept (`charts/*/resources-entry-map.json`) come with it.
items.rationale: Ran the tool end to end from this environment against the live estate on 2026-09-26: `recommend_resources.py report <scratch>` cloned 48 deploy repos from the registry (/work/ArgoCDDeploy/releases/values.yaml), read Prometheus at prometheus.home, wrote 31 patches (`31 of 48 deploy repos would change`) into <dir>/report, and listed 4451 not-placed containers (4425 are jenkins-prd build pods). The script names HelmCharts only in its docstring; the nine maps are in support/recommend-resources/resources-entry-maps/ (entry counts equal HelmCharts' charts/*/resources-entry-map.json; step-ca's is step-certificates.json). Values files written are config/<stage>/values.yaml (grafana: config/prd/values.yaml).
evidence: python3 support/recommend-resources/recommend_resources.py report /work/scratch/029-t1/rr -> '48 deploy repos', '31 of 48 deploy repos would change'
ls support/recommend-resources/resources-entry-maps -> 9 maps, entry counts match HelmCharts'

items.area: R5 — the report the operator reads and overrules
items.description: "I need a report to make it clear what's going to be pushed. I need to see what changed, and I need to be able to overrule stuff. It'd be good if reading and writing of this report is scripted." / "make it easy to mass delete stuff." How the report works: (1) step one writes one plain unified-diff patch file per deploy repo into a report directory; (2) the operator deletes a file to skip that app, or edits hunks to overrule them; (3) step two applies what is left to the clones, commits locally, and shows the result. Nothing is pushed by default. The phase proved step one against the live estate and step two into scratch clones.
items.rationale: Ran both steps against scratch clones. Step one wrote one unified-diff patch per deploy repo (# preamble listing each change, then git diff). I deleted NewsfilterDeploy.patch and edited GrafanaDeploy.patch's memory hunk from 160Mi to 192Mi, then ran `apply <dir>`: 30 local commits (one repo skipped because its patch was deleted), NewsfilterDeploy left at its origin commit with a clean tree, GrafanaDeploy's config/prd/values.yaml reads `memory: 192Mi`, and `apply` printed `git -C <clone> push origin main` commands without pushing (origin/main..HEAD is the one local commit; no remote changed).
evidence: apply after deleting NewsfilterDeploy.patch and editing Grafana's hunk -> 30 commits; Grafana 192Mi; Newsfilter unchanged; push commands printed, nothing pushed

items.area: R5 — recommendations keyed on the resolved chart
items.description: recommend-resources takes each app's chart from the resolved chart, never from a directory name. The resolved chart is the deploy repo's own chart, or the registry's upstream chart at the stage's pinned version. The old tool keyed on the config directory name, the mis-keying at HelmCharts `tools/chart_tools/recommend_resources.py:161-222`. Its recommendation policy is unchanged from the old tool: a 7-day window, p75 CPU and p90 working-set memory (`recommend_resources.py:73-121`), and the same rounding.
items.rationale: Policy: the two rounding functions (`round_cpu_recommendation`, `round_mem_recommendation`) compared with HelmCharts' by exec of both over 0..19999: 0 differences; `percentile()` returns numpy's linear-method values on test inputs (p90 [1..5]=4.6, p75 [1..4]=3.25); NUM_DAYS=7, p75 CPU, p90 max working-set memory (same PromQL). Keying: the not-placed list and patches name the resolved chart, e.g. `argocd-prd ... (chart argocd)`; grafana's memory 157Mi measured -> 160Mi (next quarter power of two); upstream apps take `upstream.chart` at the stage's pinned version, local apps the deploy repo's chart/Chart.yaml name (code: `resolve_chart`, recommend_resources.py:127-131). Not proven by a mutation of my own: the local-chart name keying is one of the two paths close-out S19 says the unit suite does not pin.
evidence: ast-extracted round_cpu_recommendation/round_mem_recommendation, old vs new over range(20000): 0 diffs

items.area: R6 — the registry lives in ArgoCDDeploy, Argo CD native
items.description: "Move the Argo CD registry out of HelmCharts (a slice; revisits D21/D22)." Per the D2 ruling ("Target state can be Argo CD native"), ArgoCDDeploy holds the registry as one values file, and a small chart renders one plain Application per app-stage from it. The file carries the 50 live entries and nothing else. Each entry is `repo`, an optional `upstream: {repo, chart}`, an optional `syncOptions`, and `stages:`, where each stage may set `autoSync` (default true), `targetRevision` (default `main`) and, for upstream apps, `version`. None of these carry over: `reconciler`, `deployed`, the per-stage file tree, the ApplicationSet templating, `templatePatch`.
items.rationale: ArgoCDDeploy `releases/` renders 50 Applications (`helm template releases releases -n argocd-prd | grep -c '^kind: Application$'` = 50), one per app-stage, from values.yaml alone: top key `apps`, 48 apps / 50 app-stages, 9 upstream, syncOptions on cloudnative-pg and external-secrets, autoSync false only on argocd/prd, kubecoder dev {} + prd {targetRevision: prd}; entry keys are only repo/upstream/syncOptions/stages, stage keys only autoSync/targetRevision/version; no reconciler, deployed, per-stage tree or ApplicationSet-side templating in the registry. releases/templates/applications.yaml is one plain Application per app-stage (finalizer, hook parameters, `hasKey` autoSync default true, upstream if/else).
evidence: cexec iac helm template releases releases -n argocd-prd -> 50 Applications

items.area: R6 — key validation and tests moved, no check lost
items.description: "...and move the registry's key validation, its tests..." A `values.schema.json` makes Helm refuse to render a bad registry entry, and ArgoCDDeploy's render test proves it. No coverage is lost. Every check HelmCharts makes on an Argo entry today has a named successor in the schema or the render test: the allowlist in `tools/deploy/deploy_cli/release.py:16-31`, and `origin/main` `tests/test_prd_tree.py:94-147` (booleans, the pvginkel repo prefix, a non-empty targetRevision, a complete upstream block, Argo's own entry never auto-syncing). The per-Application assertions in `tests/render-chart.py:504-652` hold for the rendered Applications.
items.rationale: Fed the chart bad registries with `helm template --set`: non-boolean autoSync, a repo outside github.com/pvginkel, an empty targetRevision, an empty upstream chart, argocd autoSync true, an upstream stage without version, a `reconciler` key, a `deployed` key, an empty version: all nine exit 1 with `values don't meet the specifications of the schema`; a valid new app is accepted. Each named old check has its successor in releases/values.schema.json (booleans -> autoSync boolean; pvginkel prefix -> repo pattern; non-empty targetRevision -> minLength; complete upstream -> required repo+chart and version per stage; Argo never auto-syncs -> apps.argocd const false; release.py's allowlist -> additionalProperties false). The per-Application assertions run over the rendered registry in tests/render-chart.py (green in the driver's sweep; ok: 'the registry renders 50 Applications into argocd-prd'). Mutation of my own: see V13.
evidence: helm template releases releases -n argocd-prd --set <bad> x9 -> rc=1 schema refusal; valid entry -> rc=0
tests/render-chart.py control run: 'ok: the registry renders 50 Applications into argocd-prd'

items.area: R6 — every state of ArgoCDDeploy is safe to sync
items.description: No commit on ArgoCDDeploy's `main` deletes an Application or cascade-deletes an ApplicationSet when synced, at any moment, with prune or without. The ApplicationSets and `releases` never both own the Applications. The ApplicationSets carry a prune guard, and one stage-level setting chooses them or `releases`; at the end of the run it chooses the ApplicationSets. `releases` behaves as follows. In steady state it auto-syncs without prune and without self-heal, so a deleted entry waits for the operator's prune (D27 amended). It comes up at the switch without syncing on its own. Deleting or pruning it never deletes an Application. The render test proves each state renders what `attachments/registry-switch.md` says.
items.rationale: Rendered `chart/` with config/prd/values.yaml at the pre-slice base (307d94f) and at HEAD (S1): the diff is exactly the two `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false` annotations on the ApplicationSets. With `--set releases.owner=releases` (S3) the object set differs from base by two ApplicationSets gone and Application/releases added; that Application has source path releases on ArgoCDDeploy main, destination in-cluster/argocd-prd, project releases, no finalizer, no syncPolicy (autoSync false). Mutations of a scratch copy, each turning tests/render-chart.py red with a named FAIL: (a) removing the Prune=false annotation ('releases-local carries annotations None, not the prune guard alone ... (D64)'); (b) adding a finalizer and prune: true to releases ('S3: releases carries finalizers ...', 'S4: releases renders syncPolicy ... it prunes and self-heals'). The unmutated copy passes and prints `renders registry-switch position S1`. Live: argocd-prd is still Synced at 307d94f, the ApplicationSets carry no annotation, and 50 Applications remain after the push (nothing polls).
evidence: diff of helm template argocd-prd chart (base 307d94f vs HEAD): only the 2 Prune=false annotations
helm template ... --set releases.owner=releases: ApplicationSets removed, Application/releases added
scratch mutations: guard dropped -> 2 FAIL; finalizer+prune -> 3 FAIL; control -> ok
kubectl get application argocd-prd -> Synced rev=307d94f after the push; ApplicationSets ann empty

items.area: R6 — the switch runbook
items.description: An operator runbook in Ansible's `docs/runbooks/` walks the hand-over in this order: a rehearsal on a throwaway ApplicationSet plus Application; ArgoCDDeploy's relay webhook; the equivalence check; guarding the ApplicationSets (`Prune=false`); orphan-deleting them (`kubectl delete applicationset … --cascade=orphan`); the equivalence check again, right before the flip; flipping the setting; syncing `argocd-prd`, which creates `releases`; reading `releases`' diff, which must show tracking metadata only; syncing `releases`; turning on its automated sync; and, last, removing the docs' notes that a procedure is owed until the registry switch has run. Each step gives the operator's command and what they must see before going on. Per the fix-forward ruling, the runbook has no way back to the ApplicationSets and says that a failure past the orphan-delete is fixed forward on `releases`; the rehearsal proves the forward path only. The runbook ends with the list of what is dead after the switch. The webhook step is needed because ArgoCDDeploy's only GitHub hook delivers to Jenkins (`gh api repos/pvginkel/ArgoCDDeploy/hooks`, 2026-09-26), so without it a registry push would reach no Argo component (D6).
items.rationale: Read /work/Ansible/docs/runbooks/registry-switch.md (442 lines): the eleven steps are in the required order (1 rehearsal a-f, 2 webhook, 3 equivalence, 4 guard, 5 orphan-delete, 6 check again, 7 flip, 8 read the diff, 9 sync, 10 automated sync, 11 remove the owed notes and mark the records), each with its command and 'You should see'; 'No way back' states fix forward and forbids reverting the flip; the list of what is dead after the switch closes it. Spot checks against the live estate: the steps' `sed` patterns match single lines in config/prd/values.yaml (`  owner: applicationsets` :196, `  autoSync: false` :198, no other autoSync line); the webhook leaf `credentials.leaves.webhook` is eso/prd/argocd/prd/webhook; scripts/bao-login.sh exists; `gh api repos/pvginkel/ArgoCDDeploy/hooks` returns one hook, Jenkins' (id 683106027); step 3's command form runs and prints 0 differing; argocd-prd has no syncPolicy (manual) so `argosync` is the only way it syncs; the live AppProject releases admits the rehearsal's destinations (*-tst, *-prd), source (github.com/pvginkel/*) and Namespace. Step 11's grep finds six notes (five in argocd.md, one in argo_migrate.py). The rehearsal and the switch themselves are the operator's (V15).
evidence: git grep -n -i 'owed until the registry switch has run' -- ':!docs/runbooks/registry-switch.md' -> 6 hits
kubectl get appproject releases -o jsonpath={.spec} (destinations, sourceRepos, clusterResourceWhitelist)

items.area: R6 — the switch done, no Application recreated
items.description: After the operator's switch, `releases` owns the 50 Applications. Each keeps its uid, creation timestamp and spec. No ApplicationSet remains. A registry push to ArgoCDDeploy refreshes `releases` through its webhook, and nothing polls.
items.owed_after: the operator's registry switch, run from P6's runbook (including ArgoCDDeploy's relay webhook)
items.rationale: The operator's registry switch ran on 2026-09-28 (Ansible docs/runbooks/registry-switch.md steps 1-11, run with Claude). Step 5 orphan-deleted both ApplicationSets; step 9's `apps` diff against the step-3 snapshot added only `releases` itself, so all 50 Applications kept uid and creation time; 50 of 50 carry the tracking id `releases:argoproj.io/Application:argocd-prd/<name>`; registry-equivalence reported only `ONLY LIVE releases` (50 rendered, 51 live, 1 differing), so every spec is unchanged. Pushes 6831e85 and 3d3d466 moved argocd-prd's and releases' sync revision within ~9s with no manual refresh (webhook). Close-out A1.
evidence: kubectl get applicationsets.argoproj.io -n argocd-prd -> No resources found (2026-09-28)
releases syncPolicy after step 10: automated prune=false selfHeal=false, retry limit 3 backoff 30s x2; releases Synced at 3d3d466

items.area: R6 — argo_migrate.py's register, flip and autosync
items.description: "...and `argo_migrate.py`'s register, flip and autosync steps." `flip` and `autosync` edit ArgoCDDeploy's registry file (a local commit, comments preserved) instead of HelmCharts' `release.yaml`. Every read the tool makes of an app-stage's registry entry uses the new registry: whether it is on Argo (`support/argo-migrate/argo_migrate.py:88-99`, `:935-937`), its upstream pin (`:444-450`) and its `syncOptions`. Per the D2 ruling (a premise correction to R6's wording, accepted by the operator at review r1), `register` never touched the registry: it edits only Architecture's `pipeline-producers.yaml` (`:1521-1533`), so it is unchanged. The tool's reads of HelmCharts' charts and configs stay.
items.rationale: argo_migrate.py: REGISTRY = releases/values.yaml (:58); `App.entry` reads the registry (:126), `on_argo` is `stage in entry.stages` (:130); registry_apps() reads ARGOCD_DEPLOY/REGISTRY (:1572); flip/autosync call registry_commit -> registry_flip/registry_autosync -> a local ArgoCDDeploy commit of REGISTRY only (:1712-1731); register is unchanged (edits only Architecture's pipeline-producers.yaml, and P2's removal of helm-charts does not touch it). The text edits are covered by test_registry.py (green in the driver's sweep, python3 -m unittest discover -s support/argo-migrate). Not run live by me: flip/autosync against a scratch ArgoCDDeploy (the tool hard-codes /work/ArgoCDDeploy), relying on P7's recorded scratch proof plus the unit tests; close-out S18 records the untested reads.

items.area: R6 — the decision records match the native registry
items.description: AnsibleSpecs `argo-cd/` (`decisions.md`, `design.md`, `phases.md`) records the Argo CD native registry. Every decision it changes is amended or superseded in place. The rulings name D20, D21, D23 and D27 (the prune-less `releases`), and D22's upgrade path, which is recorded as not taken. The decisions whose mechanism moves are also amended or superseded: D6, D24, D38, D39 (registration is a push to ArgoCDDeploy) and D62. `phases.md`'s endgame items are brought in line.
items.rationale: AnsibleSpecs argo-cd/decisions.md carries dated 2026-09-26 amendment or supersession notes in place for D6 (:59), D20 (superseded, after :199-205), D21 (:217), D22 (:228, upgrade path not taken), D23 (:240), D24 (:250), D27 (:362), D38 (:564), D39 (:581), D44 (:782), D62 (:968), plus D63/D64/D65 as new records and O2 closed (:1001). design.md and phases.md describe the native registry with the ApplicationSets as the until-the-switch state; phases.md's endgame item states the switch as the operator's step, owed, from the runbook path. The estate register's tool split (decisions.md:35, :48) names deploy repos and Argo CD.

items.area: R7 — docs describe the Argo CD deploy path
items.description: "Docs that still describe HelmCharts as the deploy path: Ansible's CLAUDE.md, `docs/live-infra-access.md` and about a dozen runbooks." These docs describe the Argo CD deploy path (deploy repos, ArgoCDDeploy's registry) instead: Ansible's `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/live-infra-access.md`, the runbooks the rulings list, `docs/design-philosophy.md`, the `baseline`, `microk8s` and `microceph` role READMEs, and the `root` description in `.kubecoder/project.yaml`. In AnsibleSpecs, the estate register's tool split (`decisions.md:35`, `:48`) is covered too. Historical mentions stay historical. Per the docs-across-the-switch ruling, no doc calls the new registry live before the operator's switch. Each procedure that depends on which registry is live carries a one-line note that it is owed until the registry switch has run: registering an app (`docs/runbooks/argocd.md:218`), the handover flip (`:412`) and the cold-boot bootstrap (`:681-685`). The switch runbook's last step finds and removes those notes.
